assertion.name: TRIO
assertion.notes: Illustrates the cytoskeletal/Rho GTPase module: TRIO is a Dbl-family guanine nucleotide exchange factor that activates Rac1 and controls actin dynamics in developing neurons. Included here with two explicit caveats that make it instructive rather than clean. First, the best-characterised TRIO series reports microcephaly and dysmorphism alongside the ID, so this gene-disease pair sits on the syndromic side of an unstable boundary. Second, that series includes an autosomal dominant frameshift that SEGREGATED through a family as well as de novo missense variants, demonstrating that the class is not exclusively de novo. Both caveats argue against treating "autosomal dominant" and "de novo" as synonyms. A third caveat is that the head-size feature is not directionally fixed: TRIO-related disease includes both MRD44 with microcephaly and MRD63 with macrocephaly. The dedicated TRIO-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder entry now models that domain-resolved, RAC1-direction-dependent split and is the canonical home for TRIO variants and mechanisms. TRIO is retained here only as a boundary exemplar, not as a clean non-syndromic gene; the cephalic and dysmorphic findings illustrate why umbrella AD-NSID membership is partial (see GitHub issue 6041).

selected_evidence.snippet: Trio is a Dbl family guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) and a major regulator of neuronal development, controlling actin cytoskeleton dynamics by activating the GTPase Rac1.

assertion.name: C10orf71
assertion.association: Autosomal dominant causal pathogenic variant. C10orf71 encodes an intrinsically disordered, cardiomyocyte-specific protein also reported as the z-disc protein CEFIP. Frameshift variants were identified in a large family with eight affected members and in four further loss-of-function carriers across two sporadic DCM cohorts. Null cardiomyocytes lose contractile function while sarcomere structure stays intact, so the lesion is contractile rather than structural.

selected_evidence.snippet: Importantly, CEFIP was located at the z-disc and was up-regulated in several models of cardiomyopathy.

assertion.name: EMD
assertion.association: X-linked causal pathogenic variant. EMD encodes emerin, an inner nuclear membrane protein whose loss classically causes Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy type 1, curated separately in this knowledge base. A distinct cardiac-only phenotype exists: the c.23C>G p.Ser8Trp missense variant co-segregated with DCM in six hemizygous males aged 36 to 50 with no muscular dystrophy, with greatly reduced myocardial emerin. The authors of that study note that before it the evidence for isolated DCM as an EMD phenotype was insufficient, so this gene is recorded here as an emerging rather than an established nonsyndromic DCM gene.

selected_evidence.snippet: Although an association with isolated dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) has been suggested, evidence is currently insufficient to verify the gene-disease association.

value.description: The severe end of the L1CAM-related L1 syndrome spectrum (which also includes MASA syndrome / X-linked complicated spastic paraplegia type 1 and X-linked complicated corpus callosum agenesis). Affected males are born with severe hydrocephalus, adducted thumbs and spasticity, and hypoplasia or aplasia of the corticospinal tracts is near-constant at autopsy. value.description: Recurrent protein-truncating founder variant in CC2D1A on 19p13.12, identified in nine consanguineous families with SEVERE non-syndromic intellectual disability. value.description: Biallelic variants in MAN1B1 (alpha-1,2-mannosidase) at 9q34.3, a second glycosylation entry point alongside TUSC3. assertion.notes: PRRX1 (paired related homeobox 1) is one of the two established causal genes. Reported variants include frameshift and other loss-of-function alleles; a biallelic form has been reported in an affected infant. PRRX1 mutations were identified in 4 of the ~32 genetically tested patients compiled in the 2021 review. PRRX1 is also implicated in a much milder, incompletely penetrant craniosynostosis phenotype.
